items.description: Debloat any Android or Google TV over Wi-Fi and get an Apple TV-style home.
items.readme:
cleanyour.tv · The prompt · 54 TV lists · 12 built on it · The tweet

Strip the bloatware from any Android TV or Google TV over Wi-Fi, and replace the ad-filled home screen with a clean launcher that looks like an Apple TV. **No root, no cable, nothing uninstalled, and a one-line restore if you change your mind.**

54 TVs with tested lists  ·  23 brands  ·  12 languages  ·  280 KB launcher

![Before: stock Google TV home with a sponsored ad. After: the Clean Your TV launcher](docs/stock-vs-new-side.jpg) > Vibe coded my parents' TV this afternoon! It was showing a sponsored ad before you could even get > to Netflix. Gave Claude Code the model number, it found the TV on wifi, removed 25 Xiaomi packages > and wrote a new launcher. Looks like an Apple TV now lol. > > [@gathint, 17 October 2026](https://x.com/gathint/status/2111379569030939102). The replies are where > most of the TV lists here came from. The repo was called tv-vibehack until the 19th; old links work. ## How it works Android TVs have the same debug bridge as Android phones. Switch on USB debugging in the TV's developer options, allow your computer once, and the rest is standard Android tooling: 1. **Back up** the list of installed packages and settings. 2. **Disable** the manufacturer's telemetry, ad services, content rows and preloaded junk with `pm disable-user`. Nothing is uninstalled, so a restore script can undo every step. 3. **Install** a small native launcher and make it the default home screen. The bloat differs by brand, so the prompt has your coding assistant discover it on your TV and ask before touching anything you might use. ## Quick start You need a computer on the same Wi-Fi as the TV and a coding assistant with shell access (Claude Code or similar). | | | |---|---| | **1. On the TV** | Settings → Device Preferences → About → press OK on **Build** seven times → back → Developer options → **USB debugging** on. If you see a Network or ADB debugging toggle, turn that on too. Keep the TV on. | | **2. On your computer** | Paste [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md) into your assistant and fill in your TV model. | | **3. Follow along** | Accept "Allow USB debugging?" on the TV, then answer the checklist: which apps you use, which four go in the dock, whether to keep the voice assistant, Chromecast and updates. | The assistant backs up, debloats, builds and installs the launcher, and checks each step with screenshots pulled from the TV. With this repo as context it takes about fifteen minutes. ## What you get - **A pitch-black home** with a dock of your four favourite apps in a rounded band, where Apple TV puts it. - **A top shelf** naming the focused app in large type, with an ambient glow in a colour taken from its artwork. - **The rest of your apps in a grid** that slides up when you press Down. - **One floating glass highlight** that springs from tile to tile. The focused tile lifts and shows its name. - **Three frosted buttons**: Inputs (HDMI ports, AV, Live TV), Wi-Fi or Ethernet with the network name, Settings. - **A greeting, a thin clock and the date** in [Outfit](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Outfit), and a matching Clock screensaver. - **Themes** that change colours, wallpaper, dock and columns without a rebuild, and **module cards** that let other apps plug a tile in, only with your say-so. And a TV that stops working against you: no sponsored rows, no "Discover" nags, no analytics phoning home, no apps you never asked for. | | | |---|---| | ![The top shelf names the focused app over an ambient glow in its colour](docs/focus-2-up-netflix.png) | ![The Inputs popup: HDMI ports with what is connected, AV and Live TV](docs/inputs-menu.jpg) | | *Top shelf and ambient glow* | *Inputs: HDMI with connection state, AV, Live TV* | | ![The grid with the glass highlight on a tile and its name beneath](docs/focus-1-fancode.png) | ![The Clock screensaver: a thin clock drifting over the glow](docs/clock-screensaver.png) | | *The grid, one glass highlight, the tile's name* | *Clock screensaver, drifts so nothing burns in* | | ![The aurora theme: a wallpaper and tinted pills, pushed without a rebuild](docs/theme-aurora.jpg) | ![Six columns and a six-app dock from a theme's config.json](docs/theme-six-columns.jpg) | | *Aurora theme, pushed with `tools/theme.sh`* | *Six columns and a six-app dock, same launcher* | ## Supported TVs Anything running **Android TV** or **Google TV**. Samsung (Tizen) and LG (webOS) run different systems; see [SHOWCASE.md](SHOWCASE.md) for a webOS port. **Fire TV** takes the debloat half only, since Fire OS will not hand Home to a third-party launcher. A few China-market TCL sets refuse to install any launcher at all; their lists say so in the header. Your TV not here? The prompt discovers the bloat itself. Add your list afterwards and the next person with your model skips that step: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Doing it by hand Everything the assistant does, you can run yourself. The tools need Python 3 and nothing else. ```bash python3 -m venv tools/venv && tools/venv/bin/pip install -r tools/requirements.txt export TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 # your TV's IP address tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py --probe # model, Android version, firmware tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py 'pm list packages' # one shell command on the TV tools/disable.sh examples/xiaomi-mi-tv-4a/debloat.txt # apply a debloat list tools/restore.sh examples/xiaomi-mi-tv-4a/debloat.txt # undo it, stock launcher back TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 launcher/build-and-install.sh # build the launcher and make it Home tools/theme.sh themes/aurora # push a theme; --reset removes it ``` | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | [`tools/tv.py`](tools/tv.py) | Pure-Python ADB client: shell, batch, push, pull. Works where the stock `adb` binary is blocked. | | [`tools/b64push.py`](tools/b64push.py) | Uploads large files such as APKs in base64 chunks and verifies the checksum. | | [`tools/disable.sh`](tools/disable.sh), [`restore.sh`](tools/restore.sh) | Apply or undo a debloat list. | | [`tools/theme.sh`](tools/theme.sh) | Push a folder from [`themes/`](themes/) to the launcher and restart Home. | | [`launcher/build-and-install.sh`](launcher/build-and-install.sh) | Builds a shrunk release (about 280 KB), installs it, switches Home, and rolls back if Home does not land on it. | Debloat list paths passed to `disable.sh` and `restore.sh` are relative to the directory you run from, so your own lists can live outside the repository. Absolute paths also work. Every script has a PowerShell twin next to it. On Windows with Android Studio installed nothing else is needed: ```powershell python -m venv tools\venv; tools\venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r tools\requirements.txt powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File launcher\build-and-install.ps1 -TvHost 192.168.1.50 powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\disable.ps1 -TvHost 192.168.1.50 examples\xiaomi-mi-tv-4a\debloat.txt ``` The install scripts ask the TV which launcher owns Home and only disable one they recognise (`tvlauncher` or `launcherx`); pass `STOCK_LAUNCHER=` (`-StockLauncher`) to override, or `none` to leave it alone. ## The launcher A small native Android TV app (`com.gathin.tvhome`, about 280 KB installed) in plain Java with AndroidX RecyclerView and nothing heavier. Built for sets with 1 GB of RAM: no blur, no video, no network, no background services. It needs JDK 17 and Android SDK platform 34 to build; on macOS, `brew install openjdk@17 android-commandlinetools` and `sdkmanager "platforms;android-34" "build-tools;34.0.0"`. On Linux the install script finds `~/Android/Sdk` and the `java` on your PATH. - **Configure** in [`config.xml`](launcher/app/src/main/res/values/config.xml): dock order, hidden apps, the Live TV package, columns (tiles shrink from 5 up), rows under the dock, an optional VPN app for the network pill, and `reduced_motion` for TVs whose GPU cannot keep up. - **Themes** set the same keys plus a background colour and a wallpaper from a `config.json` pushed to the TV, no rebuild. Three ship in [`themes/`](themes/), documented there. - **Language** follows the TV: English, German, Spanish, Catalan, French, Russian, Serbian (Latin), Polish, Arabic, Simplified Chinese, Thai, Turkish. Android 13+ can set it for the launcher alone: `tools/tv.py 'cmd locale set-app-locales com.gathin.tvhome --locales ca'`. Russian includes the module-card approval and management screens and the VPN-off badge. - **Module cards** let any TV app declare its own tile (label, caption, glow). The launcher asks you once per app, Keep hidden by default, and remembers the answer for that app's signing key and card name. Hold OK on Settings to change your mind. How to make one: [`docs/modules.md`](docs/modules.md); the contract: [`docs/specs/card.md`](docs/specs/card.md). - **Clock screensaver**: a drifting clock over the glow, so nothing burns in. Pick "Clock" in the TV's screensaver settings, or over ADB: `tools/tv.py 'settings put secure screensaver_components com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream; settings put secure screensaver_enabled 1'` - **Remote keys**: an optional accessibility service keeps the remote's Input button working on Google TV (`INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1` at install), another fixes sticks whose Home key sends ALL_APPS and opens Settings from the remote's gear button, even one Android does not map (`HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1`, scancodes in `config.xml`). - **Navigation** is deliberate: Up and Down move one row, the top buttons never fall through to tiles and Down from them returns to the dock tile you came from, the last focused app is remembered, and installing or removing an app refreshes the tiles while Home is open. - **Artwork**: app banners load at xhdpi or better, so low-density TV UIs do not downsample them before the focus zoom. ## Restoring your TV Keep the list you applied. The restore script re-enables exactly those packages, puts the stock launcher back as Home and resets the animation scales: ```bash TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 tools/restore.sh examples//debloat.txt # Android TV TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 tools/restore.sh examples//debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx # Google TV ``` It leaves the new launcher installed (remove it from the TV's Settings → Apps if you want it gone) and does not know about packages you disabled outside the list. To switch back later, run the install script again; it works out which launcher to disable even when Home has fallen back to Android's chooser. If the TV is unreachable, its own Settings → Apps page can re-enable packages too. ## When something goes wrong The full list of things that bit us is in [docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md). The three that matter most: - **macOS blocks `adb connect`** ("No route to host") under Local Network privacy. `tools/tv.py` avoids the binary. - **Disable the stock launcher only after the new one is installed and running**, or Home lands on a factory test app. The install script orders this for you. - **On Google TV the setup wizard** (`com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith`) can take Home and crash-loop the system after the stock launcher is disabled. Disable it too, and list it in your `debloat.txt` so restore brings it back. Stuck already? `tools/tv.py 'pm enable --user 0 com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx'`. ## Questions people ask **Is this safe? Can it brick the TV?** Nothing is flashed, rooted or deleted; packages are disabled in the user profile. The risk is disabling something the TV leans on, which is why lists are applied in small batches with a restore script ready. The TV's own Settings → Apps page can re-enable packages even without the tools. **What about firmware updates?** Most lists disable the update service, so updates arrive only when you re-enable it. If one lands, the worst case is a package coming back and you re-run the script. **Won't the apps break?** Streaming apps still update through the Play Store, which is left alone. The launcher just lists what is installed and launches it with intents that have been stable for a decade. **Isn't ADB access a security hole?** It is one explicit "allow this computer" tap on the TV, the same as developing an Android app. Switch USB debugging off afterwards; the launcher keeps working. **Can it block ads inside apps too?** Partly, with Android's Private DNS (Android 9 and newer). Point it at an ad-blocking resolver such as [AdGuard DNS](https://adguard-dns.io) and every app's ad and tracker domains stop resolving, system-wide, surviving reboots. The trade-off: that resolver then sees every DNS query the TV makes. ```bash tools/tv.py 'settings put global private_dns_specifier dns.adguard-dns.com' tools/tv.py 'settings put global private_dns_mode hostname' ``` It does not remove YouTube ads, which come from the same servers as the videos. If an app stops playing or the TV reports "No internet" (the resolver is down or unreachable), switch back with `tools/tv.py 'settings put global private_dns_mode opportunistic'`. **AirPlay?** Not from this repo. Chromecast built-in stays for Android phones. For iPhones, [jqssun/android-airplay-server](https://github.com/jqssun/android-airplay-server) works; an install script for it is in [PR #84](https://github.com/Gathin23/cleanyourtv/pull/84). **Can I just download the APK?** Build it with the one-line script; it takes a minute and you control what goes on your TV. No prebuilt binaries. ## Contributing The most useful contribution is your TV's debloat list, so the next person with that model does not have to rediscover it. Launcher improvements and sharper prompt wording are welcome too. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) has the format and the testing we ask for. Built something on top, a launcher, a port, a theme? Add it to [SHOWCASE.md](SHOWCASE.md), where eleven projects already live: a webOS port for LG, a Stremio shelf, a Hisense restyle, Fire TV launchers, an AirPlay installer. The people whose work is in this repo:

items.name: git-ai
items.readme:
Git designed for AI agents.

Anthropic built **Scion**, a faster version control system for coding agents, and described it in [Redesigning source control](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/redesigning-source-control): a server-centric system built for hundreds of agents that read, write and land code at the same time. Scion is internal to Anthropic and is not available to the public. So I built **gitai**: an open-source version of that design that anyone can run, and that the community can improve and maintain together. MIT licensed. Vendor neutral: the server never calls a language model, and every AI feature works with any provider, or none. gitai is an independent implementation of the publicly described design. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. --- ## Why Classic Git hosting was built for humans who clone a repository, work for hours and push once. Coding agents work differently: thousands of short-lived tasks, each touching a few files, each wanting to land in seconds, all on the same branches. Full clones, merge queues and client-side history walks become the bottleneck. Scion's answer is to move the work to the server: clients stay online and fetch only what they need, history questions are answered (and cached) by the server, changes land through a compare-and-swap instead of a queue, every update is an entry in a changeset log, and the repository state lives in a consistent database plus object storage so servers scale out. gitai implements these ideas, with normal Git repositories underneath. ## The Scion ideas, implemented | Scion idea | In gitai | |---|---| | **Always-online clients** that fetch exactly what they need | `ObjectService` serves single objects and sparse trees; `graft clone` and `graft sparse` materialize only the paths you ask for. | | **Source control as an API**: history runs on the server | Blame, path history, ancestry and code search run server-side and are memoized as derived data, computed once per commit. | | **Landing without a merge queue** | `UserLand` rebases a change onto the current tip and lands it with a compare-and-swap; concurrent lands on one branch are batched into a single reference update. | | **Automatic conflict resolution** | A conflicting land is resolved by a resolver you choose (any LLM provider, a deterministic tool, or none) through a versioned, vendor-neutral protocol. | | **Changeset log** | Every accepted reference update is recorded with its operation and actor in a dense, ordered log that clients list or watch live. | | **Storage core: a database and object storage, stateless servers** | Each change is a changeset in a write-ahead log in SQLite or PostgreSQL, with a compare-and-swap per reference; packs live in object storage (file, S3, GCS, Azure). Server nodes are caches that any node can rebuild, so you add nodes to scale. | | **Test after landing, revert the culprit** | `graft-verify` tests the tip, bisects a failure and reverts the change that broke it. | | **Monitoring agents ("superfans")** | Agents follow the changeset stream and report what matters to each component, also through Slack. | | **Agent-friendly review** | Reviews with semantic approval rules: a comment-only change can need fewer approvals than a logic change. | | **Agents as first-class users** | Per-agent tokens, an RPC allowlist and branch policies decide what each agent may do. | | **Strict cache tiers** | `graft-cache` caches immutable objects in daemon and regional tiers, verifying every object. | ## Architecture ``` agents, CI jobs, sparse workspaces graft CLI / Go SDK | v gRPC +-------------------------------------------------+ | graft-cache (optional daemon and cache tiers) | +------------------------+------------------------+ v +---------------------------------------------------------------+ | gitai server (any number of nodes) | | land - objects - changesets - derived data - search - review | | write path: changeset + compare-and-swap per reference | +-----------+--------------------------------+------------------+ | | v v +-----------------------+ +-----------------------------+ | SQLite / PostgreSQL | | object storage | | changeset WAL, refs, | | content-addressed packs | | changelog, reviews | | (file, S3, GCS, Azure) | +-----------------------+ +-----------------------------+ \ / local Git repositories = caches any node can rebuild ``` Details: [ARCHITECTURE.md](doc/graft/ARCHITECTURE.md) and [STORAGE.md](doc/graft/STORAGE.md). ## Quick start Requirements: Linux or macOS, Go 1.26, a C toolchain, Meson and Ninja (the build compiles a bundled Git). ```shell git clone https://github.com/feder-cr/git-ai.git cd git-ai make build # server, CLI and tools into _build/bin examples/graft/quickstart.sh # a server, a cache daemon, two agents and a land, in a temporary directory ./_build/bin/graft # the CLI and its commands ``` To run your own server, adapt [`examples/graft/config.toml`](examples/graft/config.toml) and start it with `_build/bin/gitaly serve config.toml`. To put the repository state in a database and object storage, add a `[graft.storage]` section: start in `shadow` mode, import your repositories, then switch to `authoritative` ([STORAGE.md](doc/graft/STORAGE.md)). Inside the code the extensions are called **Graft**: the `[graft]` configuration section, the `graft` CLI, `internal/graft` and `doc/graft`. ## Documentation - [Quickstart](doc/graft/QUICKSTART.md) and [configuration reference](doc/graft/CONFIGURATION.md) - [Architecture](doc/graft/ARCHITECTURE.md) and the [storage core](doc/graft/STORAGE.md) - [Landing and batching](doc/graft/LAND-BATCHING.md), [conflict resolution](doc/graft/RESOLVE.md), [derived data](doc/graft/DERIVED.md) - [Review](doc/graft/REVIEW.md), [search](doc/graft/SEARCH.md), [verification](doc/graft/VERIFY.md), [superfans](doc/graft/SUPERFAN.md) and [Slack chat](doc/graft/SUPERFAN-CHAT.md) - [Agent security](doc/graft/AGENT-SECURITY.md), [benchmarks](doc/graft/BENCH.md), [fuzzing](doc/graft/FUZZING.md) - [Limitations and roadmap](doc/graft/LIMITATIONS.md) - Design documents of each phase: [PLAN.md](doc/graft/PLAN.md) to [PLAN6.md](doc/graft/PLAN6.md) ## Status Version 0.1.0, the first public release. Everything above is implemented and covered by unit, end-to-end, multi-node, crash and fuzz tests. Interfaces may still change before 1.0. Known gaps (for example garbage collection of packs in the storage core) are listed in [LIMITATIONS.md](doc/graft/LIMITATIONS.md). ## Community gitai is meant to be maintained by its community. Open an issue to report a bug or propose an idea, start a discussion before a large design change, and send pull requests: tests and a short description of the reasoning make them easy to review. The design documents in `doc/graft/PLAN*.md` explain why things are the way they are. ## Credits and license gitai is MIT licensed, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). It started as a fork of [Gitaly](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitaly), GitLab's Git RPC server (MIT, Copyright GitLab Inc.), which provides the Git plumbing underneath; every upstream Gitaly RPC keeps working. The non-MIT `ee/` directory of upstream Gitaly is not part of this repository. Gitaly's own README is kept in [doc/UPSTREAM-GITALY.md](doc/upstream/README-GITALY.md), and third-party notices are in [NOTICE](NOTICE).

items.name: BRUTAL
items.description: A free, open source C# framework for making games, or your own game engine. Direct access to native APIs and Vulkan, with the low-level libraries around them. The foundation under Kitten Space Agency and RimWorld's Waylith engine.
items.readme: # BRUTAL Framework **A free, open source C# framework for making games, or your own game engine.** BRUTAL is a framework. You can make a game directly with it, or use it as the foundation for a separate engine. We made Kitten Space Agency directly on BRUTAL. Ludeon built their Waylith engine on it to move RimWorld off Unity. At its core is a custom interop layer giving C# direct access to native APIs and libraries. Around that we've built mathematics, memory management, strings, collections, job scheduling, logging, localization, and bindings for Vulkan, GLFW, Dear ImGui, FMOD, RakNet, Jolt and Box2D. BRUTAL doesn't make the architectural decisions for you. You write your own stack. You can use whatever NuGet packages you want, including third-party ones. It's called BRUTAL for a reason. In some ways it's much harder to use than Unity, Unreal or Godot. In other ways, particularly if you're doing something unusual, it's considerably easier. You actually have to know what you want to do first. ## Why You are only as independent as your tools are. Developers have surrendered an extraordinary amount of control over their work to companies whose interests are not necessarily aligned with their own. We're not suggesting everyone should make their own game engine. We're suggesting every developer should have the option to, without having to spend four years building the foundations first. What that means in practice: - **Free, including for commercial games.** No royalties. We don't want a percentage of your game's revenue. We ask for credit. - **Open source.** The source is here under an MIT-based licence. If one day we stop being accountable to developers, you can fork it and go your own way. - **Deliberately small.** We do a few low-level things well: interop, memory, concurrency, maths, strings, and bindings to native libraries, on the latest C# and Vulkan. We avoid allocations and unnecessary overhead and use unmanaged memory and unsafe code where it makes sense. - **A foundation, like a kernel.** Think of the Linux kernel and something like Ubuntu. It's not an exact comparison, but it gets the idea across. We provide the foundation and you build your own systems on top. ### What BRUTAL is not BRUTAL is not trying to be a general-purpose engine. There is no editor, no scene graph and no renderer, and we're not adding them. We push back on efforts to add more, because adding everything is how the industry ended up with the kind of engines we don't want to use. Pull requests that drift away from a clear purpose will be rejected. ## Projects using BRUTAL | Product | Studio | Engine (if any) | | --- | --- | --- | | [RimWorld](https://store.steampowered.com/app/294100/RimWorld/) | Ludeon Studios | Waylith | | [Kitten Space Agency](https://ahwoo.com/app/100000/kitten-space-agency/) | RocketWerkz | Direct on BRUTAL | | Torpedia | RocketWerkz | Direct on BRUTAL | | Art of the Rail | RocketWerkz | Direct on BRUTAL | | [Gruntz](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ROB5IilenZE) | RocketWerkz | Direct on BRUTAL | | Afterskies | Floating Origin Interactive | Direct on BRUTAL | Ludeon report 2 to 4 times the performance of the Unity build in their own tests, with the vast majority of existing mods still compatible. See their [Steam announcement](https://steamcommunity.com/games/294100/announcements/detail/672882362547178634). Kitten Space Agency is a free pre-alpha spaceflight simulation. It runs a solar system at real scale, and is the first major project built directly on BRUTAL. [Download it on Ahwoo](https://ahwoo.com/app/100000/kitten-space-agency/) and see the technology yourself. ## What is in the box Each top-level folder in this repository is one library, published as a NuGet package. Reference only the ones you need. | Library | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Brutal.Core` | Base types, attributes, platform detection, pointer helpers, Roslyn analyzers | | `Brutal.Interop` | The custom interop layer that gives C# direct access to native APIs | | `Brutal.Memory` | Unmanaged memory management and allocators | | `Brutal.Collections` | Collections that don't allocate | | `Brutal.Strings` | String building and handling without allocation | | `Brutal.Maths`, `Brutal.Numerics` | Vector, matrix and numeric types | | `Brutal.Concurrency` | Job system and threading | | `Brutal.Logging` | Logging | | `Brutal.Localization` | Localization | | `Brutal.Vulkan`, `Brutal.Vulkan.Abstractions`, `Brutal.Vulkan.Vma` | Vulkan bindings, abstractions and the Vulkan Memory Allocator | | `Brutal.OpenGl` | OpenGL bindings | | `Brutal.ShaderC`, `Brutal.Slang` | Shader compilation | | `Brutal.Glfw`, `Brutal.Sdl`, `Brutal.Sdl.Image`, `Brutal.Sdl.Mixer`, `Brutal.Sdl.Ttf` | Windowing and input, with SDL's image, audio mixing and font add-ons | | `Brutal.ImGui`, `Brutal.ImGui.*`, `Brutal.ImPlot` | Dear ImGui and ImPlot bindings, docking branch | | `Brutal.Render.Mesh` | Mesh utilities | | `Brutal.Texture`, `Brutal.Texture.Abstractions`, `Brutal.Ktx`, `Brutal.Gli`, `Brutal.Stb` | Texture loading, KTX and compressed formats, image decoding | | `Brutal.Gltf`, `Brutal.MeshOptimizer` | glTF loading and mesh optimisation | | `Brutal.FreeType` | Font rasterisation | | `Brutal.Fmod`, `Brutal.OpenAl` | Audio | | `Brutal.RakNet` | Networking | | `Brutal.Jolt`, `Brutal.Box2D` | 3D and 2D physics | | `Brutal.Monitor.Common`, `Brutal.Monitor.Host`, `Brutal.RenderDoc`, `Brutal.RenderDoc.ImGui` | Runtime monitoring and RenderDoc capture integration | | `Brutal.NativeFileDialog`, `Brutal.NotCurses`, `Brutal.ZLib` | Native file dialogs, terminal UI, compression | Third-party notices for each library live in its `LICENSES` folder, `Brutal.ImGui/LICENSES` say. ## Getting started ### Prerequisites - [.NET 10 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download) - A Vulkan 1.3 capable GPU with current drivers (if you render) - The [Vulkan SDK](https://vulkan.lunarg.com/) if you want validation layers while developing - Windows or Linux ### Your first window Create a project and add Core and Glfw: ```sh dotnet new console -n HelloBrutal cd HelloBrutal dotnet add package Ahwoo.Brutal.Core dotnet add package Ahwoo.Brutal.Glfw ``` Replace `Program.cs`: ```csharp using Brutal.GlfwApi; using Brutal.Numerics; if (!Glfw.Init()) throw new Exception("Failed to initialize GLFW"); Glfw.WindowHint(GlfwWindowHint.ClientApi, 0); var window = Glfw.CreateWindow(new GlfwWindow.CreateInfo { Title = "Hello BRUTAL", Size = new int2(1280, 720), }); while (!window.ShouldClose) Glfw.PollEvents(); Glfw.Terminate(); ``` ```sh dotnet run ``` That opens a window with no graphics API. What you add next is up to you: - **Rendering:** `Ahwoo.Brutal.Vulkan.Abstractions` and `Ahwoo.Brutal.Vulkan.Vma` for a Vulkan renderer, `Ahwoo.Brutal.ShaderC` to compile shaders at runtime. - **Debug UI:** `Ahwoo.Brutal.ImGui` and `Ahwoo.Brutal.ImPlot`. - **Parallelism:** `Ahwoo.Brutal.Concurrency` for the job system. - **Audio and networking:** `Ahwoo.Brutal.Fmod`, `Ahwoo.Brutal.RakNet`. Questions and "how do I" threads go on the [Guides and Help forum](https://forums.ahwoo.com/forums/brutal/guides-and-help/). ### Building from source This is the source for every published package. Project files, a solution and build scripts are coming. Until then use the NuGet packages, and use this repository to read and fork the code. ```sh git clone https://github.com/ahwootech/BRUTAL.git ``` ## Licence BRUTAL is free to use, modify and distribute, including in commercial games. There are no royalties and we don't want a percentage of your game's revenue. The licence is based on MIT with an added attribution requirement. A game or product built with BRUTAL: 1. includes the BRUTAL copyright notice in its credits screen, or equivalent (section 2.1) 2. shows the BRUTAL logo before gameplay starts (section 2.2) 3. ships `NOTICE.txt` alongside the product (section 2.3) If you don't want to do that, we can arrange a separate commercial licence. We also waive the logo requirement for non-profit projects and where displaying it would be detrimental to the application's purpose. BRUTAL is open source. There are already OSI-approved licences that allow graphical attribution. Ours is not yet OSI approved because we have not submitted it yet. We intend to, and to develop the licence with community feedback. See [LICENSE.txt](LICENSE.txt) for the full text. Third-party components keep their own licences. Section 4.0 points at the `LICENSES` folder at the root of each NuGet package; in this repository, those notices are in the `LICENSES` folder of each library that redistributes them. ## Contributing You can submit PRs and issues. We are a small team and maintaining a public framework is going to be a lot of work, so please be patient with us. We'll see what happens, assess the problems, and change our workflows as necessary. What won't change is BRUTAL's scope. Before opening a PR, read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). It covers scope, what we expect from AI-assisted contributions, the contribution grant in section 5.0 of the licence, and the sign-off every commit needs. Small changes you understand and have tested, with a clear purpose, are the ones that will get merged. - Security issues: report them privately, see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Don't open a public issue. - Conduct: [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## Community - Source: https://github.com/ahwootech/BRUTAL - NuGet packages: https://www.nuget.org/profiles/Ahwoo - Forums: https://forums.ahwoo.com/forums/brutal/ - Discord: https://discord.gg/MEuNTYbAh8 ## Credits BRUTAL was made by the RocketWerkz Enterprise team and others, named in [CONTRIBUTORS.md](CONTRIBUTORS.md). When we talk about wanting credit for BRUTAL, these are the people we are talking about. BRUTAL is Copyright (c) 2024 Ahwoo Limited.

items.name: handwired
items.description: Turn your regular JavaScript code into a neural net.
items.readme:
# Handwired

Turn your regular JavaScript code into a neural net; no training, exact, yet also fully differentiable!

## How It Works

A program's made of if-else, loops, and state. Handwired transforms them into matrix multiplication + reglu over floats. For example:

```ts
const a = 5
const result = (a > 4) ? 10 : 12
```

The above can be expressed as basic arithmetic:

```ts
const a = 5
// Math.max(0, x) is ReLU. For an integer a, above4 is 1 if a > 4, and 0 otherwise
const above4 = Math.max(0, a - 4) - Math.max(0, a - 5)
// Both branches compute, and above4 picks one
const result = above4 * 10 + (1 - above4) * 12
```

You can calculate that by hand and see that both arrive at the same result.

We then collect the + and * and relu into a giant matmul, and either run it on JS or WebGPU, for fun.

Because we basically only use these 2 primitives:
- the full program stays differentiable
- the weights don't need training since they're written manually
- existing gpu techniques, such as fusion, sparsity, reordering, have a great time optimizing such minimal primitives

This unlocks lots of funny use-cases, like:
- unfreezing the weights and train them (what does that even do? Let's find out!)
- attaching a specific frozen program to a generic neural net and train end-to-end (now a nanoGPT can do both Shakespeare and your particular UI?)
- achieving GPU-level of parallelism with JS code that was written in a traditional single-threaded way (see the JSON search demo that runs in milliseconds over 100k documents)

## Play With It

Try the demos live: https://chenglou.me/handwired/

`git clone && bun install`, then `bun start` to run them locally. Check `docs/`, `src/` and `template/` to get started! (`lab/` is a bunch of old experiments you can check or ignore)

# MacNativeGames

# English

> **Use your AI assistant to help you build the Mac app. We recommend Claude Code, Codex, or any other AI assistant you prefer.**

[English](#english) | [中文](#chinese)

## Legal

**You must own the game.** Use this project only with a copy of The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom that you bought, and with keys and system files dumped from your own Nintendo Switch. This is an independent, non-commercial project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Nintendo. The Legend of Zelda and Nintendo Switch are trademarks of Nintendo.

The repository contains no game content and distributes none: no game program, art, text, audio, shaders or keys. Everything the game needs is made on your own computer from your own files when you build the app. The app you build contains the game, so it is for your own use only; do not share it. What the repository does hold is the information needed to make the port work: the patch code, the addresses and hashes used to check your files, and the [shared shader list](docs/shader-list.md), which names shaders and bind states but contains no shader code.

Play your own copy of **The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom** natively on Apple silicon Mac, iPhone, and iPad. Bring your game file (XCI or NSP) and your `prod.keys`; one script builds a Mac app or an unsigned iPhone/iPad IPA. The iOS build requires iOS/iPadOS 26 and iPhone 14 or newer. It is not an emulator: the game's own ARM64 code runs directly on Apple chips (rewritten where the operating system requires it), the Switch system services are answered by a small host, and the game's NVN graphics are rebuilt on Metal. Nothing from the game is in this repository, and the project is not affiliated with Nintendo. Version 1.4.3 has been played on an iPhone 14 and an iPad; see [iPhone and iPad](#iphone-and-ipad).

## Let's maintain the shader list together: no more stutter

> [!TIP]
> **Every shader in the shared list is ready before you play.** On a Mac the game does not stop to compile it, and on an iPhone or iPad nothing is missing from the picture. The more places players cover, the smoother the game gets for everyone.

The [shared shader list](docs/shader-list.md) now holds **26,832 shader variants** (23,867 shaders) from the Mac, iPhone and iPad. Every build makes them from the player's own game files, so the list holds identifiers only, never game data. Helping takes no setup:

1. **Play.** When your game meets a shader the list does not have yet, it notes it in `shader-list-contribution.txt`.
2. **On a Mac, every 500 new shaders it asks you once, before the game starts.** Click "Send": the GitHub form opens and the file is shown, ready to drag in. An iPhone or iPad never asks during play: while it is connected to the Mac that built its app (cable or the same Wi-Fi), the Mac asks instead. "Don't remind me again" stops the reminders.
3. **Everyone's next build carries them.** Nobody stutters there again.

**[Send your shaders →](https://github.com/ly05010419/MacNativeGames/issues/new?template=shader-list.yml)** · The game never uploads anything by itself.

Update history:

| Date | Platform | Update |
|---|---|---|
| Oct 19 | Mac | Key 4 switches to a true 21:9 ultrawide view and back (1.2.1, 1.4.3); the HUD keeps its shape in the middle 16:9 |
| Oct 19 | iPhone, iPad | Tested with 1.4.3: a fresh install shows the game from the first launch, without a played cache |
| Oct 19 | iPhone, iPad | Touch controls laid out like a Switch controller, with every button and both sticks |
| Oct 19 | All | The game notes the shaders the shared list lacks; on a Mac, every 500 it asks to send them in a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/ly05010419/MacNativeGames/issues/new?template=shader-list.yml) |
| Oct 19 | All | One shared [shader list](docs/shader-list.md); the build reads every shader in the game data (15,266 prepared for 1.4.3) |
| Oct 19 | Mac | 1.2.1 support (the most widely used update), with the same build command |
| Oct 19 | Mac | FPS, shader and load readings and the shortcut reminder in one small box in the window's top-right corner (`TOTK_HUD=corners` keeps the old layout) |
| Oct 18 | iPhone, iPad | IPA build target |
| Oct 18 | Mac | 1.4.3 support and shader prewarming: the title screen waits only for its own shaders (about 2 seconds), the rest warm in the background |
| Oct 17 | Mac | 1.0.0 and 1.1.2 support; no first-launch shader prewarming yet, so new scenes could stutter |

**Stuttering when you first start playing or enter a new scene is expected while new shaders compile—don't be surprised.** Performance typically improves as the cache warms up, and every shader the [shared list](#lets-maintain-the-shader-list-together-no-more-stutter) gains is one nobody stutters on again.

## Audio fix

Streamed music and dialogue lookup for `content://Sound/...` paths has been fixed. Opening dialogue and music were verified locally on version 1.0.0; other versions and scenes still need validation. The renderer also runs all known audio effect types and starts output after 20 ms of queued audio (2026-10-18). Rebuild your app with the original game inputs to apply the fix. See [audio troubleshooting and validation](docs/audio-troubleshooting.md) for details.

## Local testing

Tested on **MacBook Air M4 and Mac mini M4**. Local testing has collected **8,582 shaders**, with performance at approximately **90 FPS after shader warm-up, reaching 120 FPS in menus**.

Those are earlier local observations, not a stable frame-rate promise for every version or scene. Version 1.4.3 measurements and compilation stalls are recorded separately in [the test notes](docs/v1.4.3-port.md).

Shaders are automatically collected, compiled and cached as you play. Returning to previously visited scenes typically brings noticeable improvements in frame rates and smoothness because cached shaders can be reused. **8,582 is the number collected so far in local testing, not the game's total shader count or a collection limit**; the cache continues to grow as you explore.

**Shader prewarming on the first launch:** Building the app prepares shaders from your selected game data and includes them in the app: every shader in the game data for its default bind state, plus every variant named in the [shared shader list](docs/shader-list.md). Even with an empty user cache, the first launch imports these shaders. Only what the title screen itself uses is warmed before the first frame (about 2 seconds once macOS has compiled them before); the rest, together with compatible entries in the pipeline manifest, warms in the background behind the title, and the first trip into the world waits up to 15 seconds for it. No preliminary play session or manual cache copy is needed. The current 1.4.3 build prepares 15,266. Building the app also compiles them for your Mac's GPU. With Xcode's Metal toolchain installed they are compiled into the app (about 6 minutes on an M4 for 1.4.3) and work wherever the app goes. Without it they are compiled into macOS's Metal cache (a few minutes), and Metal finds them only while the game runs from where the app was built: if you move the app afterwards (to /Applications, for example), if macOS clears the cache (it does when the system disk fills up), or if another program was using Metal's cache while the app was built (a running game, for example; the build says so), the background warm-up compiles them again, which takes a few minutes, and new scenes can stutter until it finishes. To place the app elsewhere, build it there with `-o`; see [preparation and test details](docs/first-launch-shaders.md). Places no player has reported yet can still need new variants, which the Mac compiles while you play (a short stutter the first time). Playing adds them to your local cache, which is reused on later launches. The game also notes every variant the shared list does not have yet in `shader-list-contribution.txt`, and every 500 of them asks once whether to send the file in a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/ly05010419/MacNativeGames/issues/new?template=shader-list.yml) ("Send" opens the form and shows the file to drag in). It never uploads anything by itself. With git, you can also merge your cache and open a pull request, as [the list's guide](docs/shader-list.md) explains. The list holds shader and pipeline identifiers only, never game data, saves or compiled shaders; every build makes the shaders from the player's own game files.


## What you need

- A Mac with Apple silicon and **macOS 26** or later (the graphics use Metal 4); macOS 27 is supported. 16 GB of memory or more is recommended.
- About **25 GB** of free disk space for the work folder, in addition to your game file. Keep the output app on the **same APFS volume** to share the large data files through cloning. If cloning is unavailable or the app is on another volume, allow roughly **17 GB more** for the app copy.
- Your Tears of the Kingdom **base game 1.0.0** (`0100F2C0115B6000`) as an **XCI or NSP**, and your `prod.keys`. To build **1.1.2, 1.2.1 or 1.4.3**, supply its separate cumulative update as NSP or NSZ with `--update`; no intermediate update is required. NSZ is decompressed and its NCA hashes are verified before extraction. DLC and combined packages are unsupported.
- For NSP: its common ticket must be included unless the NCAs are rights-free. NSPs do not contain system shared fonts: supply an unpacked firmware NCA directory with `--firmware`, or previously extracted fonts with `--shared-fonts`. The six fonts are checked against this project’s reference dump; a valid BFTTF font from another firmware version is accepted and bound by its own bytes. Valid fonts already in the work folder are reused.

## Build the app

**1. Tools** (once): Xcode command line tools and [Homebrew](https://brew.sh). An internet connection is needed to install build dependencies and fetch pinned sources:

```sh
xcode-select --install
brew install opus libvpx python@3.14
```

For an iPhone/iPad build, install full **Xcode 26 or later** (including the iOS and Metal toolchains), then install the additional tools:

```sh
brew install xcodegen cmake ninja
```

Optional: with Xcode's Metal toolchain (`xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain`), the build compiles the startup shaders into the app. It finds an Xcode kept outside `/Applications` too (on another volume, or set `DEVELOPER_DIR`). Without it, the build compiles them into the Mac's own Metal cache for the app's location instead, which does not move with the app: after moving it, the first launch compiles them again.

**2. Download or clone this repository**, then open Terminal in its `MacNativeGames` folder and run the script with your game file and keys:

```sh
python3.14 build_app.py ~/Games/totk.xci -k ~/keys/prod.keys
```

For an NSP, supply the shared fonts too:

```sh
python3.14 build_app.py ~/Games/totk.nsp -k ~/keys/prod.keys --firmware ~/Games/firmware
# Or reuse the six .bfttf files from a previous build:
python3.14 build_app.py ~/Games/totk.nsp -k ~/keys/prod.keys --shared-fonts /path/to/TOTK_build/totk/extracted/firmware/shared-fonts
```

`--firmware` accepts a directory of `.nca` files (unpack a firmware archive first), or an installed firmware `registered` directory. `--shared-fonts` accepts the extracted directory containing `0-standard.bfttf` through `5-nintendo-extension.bfttf`. No fonts or keys are downloaded. For an XCI, fonts are read from its system update partition by default; if that partition is missing, use one of these font options too. By default both input formats produce a macOS `.app`.

To build an unsigned iPhone/iPad IPA instead, add `--platform ios` and use an `.ipa` output path:

```sh
python3.14 build_app.py ~/Games/totk.xci -k ~/keys/prod.keys --platform ios -o ~/Games/TOTK.ipa
```

Add `--update ~/Games/1.4.3.nsp` to select an update, and keep the `--firmware` or `--shared-fonts` option when the base game is an NSP. The first iOS build downloads and compiles device versions of Opus and libvpx and compiles the shader seed for iOS, so it needs an internet connection and substantial temporary disk space (allow at least **45 GB free** for a fresh base build, or **60 GB** for a fresh build with an update). The resulting IPA is unsigned: sign and install it with your sideloading tool, keeping its entitlements (it uses the increased memory limit). iOS/iPadOS 26 and iPhone 14 or newer are required. See [iPhone and iPad](#iphone-and-ipad) for what has been tested.

Without `-o`, the selected output appears next to the game file (`Tears of the Kingdom.app` on Mac or `Tears of the Kingdom.ipa` for iOS). Before full shader preparation was added, a local clean base-1.0.0 Mac build took about 6 minutes on an M4 Mac mini (this is not a timing estimate for the current build; hardware, disk and network conditions affect the time): about a minute each to rewrite the main code module and to decrypt the 17 GB of game data, and two to three minutes for macOS to check the finished app once. The current build then also prepares the startup shaders (about 3 minutes for 1.4.3 on an M4) and compiles them for your GPU (a few more minutes; without the Metal toolchain this step is skipped, with a message, while a game is running). A Mac build needs no .NET or CMake, and the finished game needs no Python: its shader translator is a native program that comes with this repository (`games/totk/prebuilt`). Every intermediate file is in a work folder next to the game file (`TOTK_build`, or `--work`); running the script again reuses what is already done.

The extracted code modules, rewritten modules, RomFS and shared fonts are checked against the selected version's `games/totk/assets/expected-v1.0.0.json`, `expected-v1.1.2.json`, `expected-v1.2.1.json` or `expected-v1.4.3.json`; the prebuilt shader translator has its own SHA-256 check. A mismatch stops the build, with one exception: a different genuine retail dump of the same version is accepted — its `main.npdm` is checked by Nintendo’s ACID signature (`npdm_signed()`) instead of the pinned hash, and its firmware’s shared fonts are checked for a valid BFTTF structure and bound by their actual SHA-256. Key values are never printed.

Signing and verifying a large updated app can add several minutes. Keep the build running while it continues to report progress.

**3. Play:** open the app from Finder. The build starts the launcher in `--check` mode, which checks that the game executable exists and allows macOS to perform its first-launch checks; it does not run a gameplay test. You can keep the app where it was built or move it to `/Applications`; the first start after a move compiles the shaders again in the background (macOS's Metal cache does not follow the app to its new place), so to keep it in `/Applications`, build it there with `-o`. Copying it to a different volume can use additional disk space and trigger another macOS check, during which no window may appear. The first game launch verifies the game data (about 20 seconds in local testing). Newly encountered shaders can cause stutters; cached shaders reduce this work on later visits.

### iPhone and iPad

Version 1.4.3 has been played on an **iPhone 14 (iOS 26.6.1)** and an **iPad with the A16 chip (iPadOS 26.7.1)**, both signed with a personal development team in Xcode. Versions 1.0.0, 1.1.2 and 1.2.1 have not been tested on iOS.

- **First launch:** the app checks the game data (about 15 seconds) and imports the shaders it carries, with a progress bar. On an iPhone 14 this takes about 3 minutes before the title appears. Later launches show the title in about 8 seconds.
- **Picture:** the game runs in handheld mode, as a Switch does without its dock: 1280×720.
- **Shaders:** an iPhone or iPad cannot translate shaders while playing. A draw whose shader variant the app does not carry is skipped, so objects can be missing in places no player has reported yet. The device records what it missed in `shader-list-contribution.txt` (Files app › On My iPhone › Tears of the Kingdom); the game never asks about it during play. While the device is connected to the Mac that built the app (cable or the same Wi-Fi), the Mac checks every 10 minutes and every 500 new shaders asks once to send the file in a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/ly05010419/MacNativeGames/issues/new?template=shader-list.yml) (`games/totk/ios/tools/shader_contrib_watch.py`, installed by the iOS build; `--no-shader-reminder` skips it, `shader_contrib_watch.py uninstall` removes it). Once merged into the [shared shader list](docs/shader-list.md), the next build carries them for everyone. With a Mac, `games/totk/ios/tools/fill_shaders.py` also translates them and sends them to the device right away.
- **Memory:** the game uses close to 4 GB on an iPhone 14, near what the phone can give it. In busy areas iOS can close the game after several minutes of play when the phone runs out of memory (seen twice on an iPhone 14, about 8 minutes in). Reducing the game's memory on iOS is the next piece of work.

## Controls

On Mac, controllers recognized by macOS (such as DualSense and Xbox controllers) are mapped to a Switch Pro Controller. PlayStation and Xbox face buttons map by position, so each one sits where the game's prompt shows it: the right button is A, the bottom B, the top X and the left Y (Circle / Cross / Triangle / Square; Xbox B / A / Y / X). Nintendo controllers map by label. `TOTK_FACE_BUTTONS=label` maps every controller by label instead. Rumble and motion require the corresponding features to be exposed by the controller and macOS; not every controller has a gyroscope. Mac keyboard mappings use physical key positions corresponding to a US layout:

| Key | Switch | | Key | Switch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W A S D | left stick | | arrow keys | right stick |
| J | A | | K, Space | B |
| I | X (jump) | | U | Y (attack) |
| Q / E | L / R | | Option / Shift | ZL / ZR |
| F T H G | d-pad left / up / right / down | | Z / C | left / right stick press |
| Return | + (menu) | | Tab, Esc | − (map) |

Controller layout (Mac): by default the face buttons follow the Switch layout by position: the right button is A, the bottom B, the top X and the left Y on every controller (Nintendo controllers by their labels, which are the same; `TOTK_FACE_BUTTONS=label` maps PlayStation and Xbox controllers by label instead). To change any button, put lines `physical = Switch [mode]` in `~/Library/Application Support/MacNativeGames/TOTK/controls.txt`; lines not given keep the default, `#` starts a comment and `none` leaves a button unused. Physical buttons are named by position: `south` `east` `west` `north` (face buttons), `l1` `r1` `l2` `r2` `l3` `r3`, `menu` (Options / Menu), `view` (Create / View), `up` `down` `left` `right` (d-pad) and `touchpad` (the touchpad click of a DualSense or DualShock 4, unused by default: `touchpad = minus` opens the Purah Pad). Switch buttons: `a` `b` `x` `y` `l` `r` `zl` `zr` `plus` `minus` `lstick` `rstick` `up` `down` `left` `right`. The optional mode says how long the Switch button is held: `hold` (default) while the physical button is down, `tap` for 400 ms after each press, and `toggle` on and off at each press, cleared when the left stick returns to center after moving, and `aim <fire button>` while the button is down except while the fire button is also down: `l2 = zr aim r2` draws the bow with L2 and shoots with R2, and R2's own line applies only while L2 is up. The default is the same as this file, which maps by position:

```
east = a
south = b
north = x
west = y
```

To run without holding a button, two lines can drive the run button: `south = b tap` (tap the bottom button again and again, as in GTA) or `l3 = b toggle` (click the stick once and move; it stops when the stick returns to center). The Switch's B is contextual: while climbing, a held B lets go of the wall, so a toggle that is still on when you climb drops the player. Release the stick before climbing, or use `tap`.

The launcher checks the file at every start and names the first bad line in an alert. Delete the file for the default layout.

Mac-only extra keys: **1** show or hide all on-screen overlays (FPS, shader count, system load and the shortcut reminder, together in one small box in the window's top-right corner; `TOTK_HUD=corners` puts the readings back in the picture's corners), **2** frame interpolation (off → 30+30 → half the refresh rate → unlimited), **3** cycle picture mode (MetalFX 2K → native 2K → off), **4** ultrawide 21:9 on / off (1.2.1 and 1.4.3: the camera sees more at the sides and the picture fills a wider window; `TOTK_ASPECT=32:9` or `3440x1440` picks another shape and starts with it on; the HUD, menus and map keep their shape in the middle 16:9 of the window, the map with black bars at the sides; markers that follow objects in the world are not moved out yet). The shortcut reminder shows the current interpolation and picture modes and refreshes twice a second in both HUD layouts. MetalFX is off by default and only starts when you select its mode with **3**; resizing the window never enables it automatically. Text entry (naming a horse) uses the Mac keyboard. iPhone/iPad uses touch controls or a compatible game controller and does not show the Mac 1/2/3/4 shortcut prompts. The touch layout follows a Switch controller: L and ZL at the top left, R and ZR at the top right, − and + between them, the d-pad on the left and A, B, X, Y on the right. The d-pad sits above the left stick and A, B, X, Y above the right stick, and L3 and R3 (stick presses) are in the bottom corners. Touch the left half away from the buttons and drag for the left stick, the right half for the camera (right stick); each stick is centred where your finger goes down. With a game controller connected the touch controls are hidden: touch the screen to show and use them, and they hide again 3 seconds after you lift your fingers.

Native 2K changes the game's composition canvas and UI to 2560×1440. The 3D scene still follows the game's separate render scaling; this does not force every internal render target to 1440p. The manual MetalFX mode also works in smaller windows and scales to the actual output size, including 4K.

Language: the game and the launcher's own text (startup screen, shader warm-up progress, overlays, keyboard prompt) follow the Mac's language. The launcher text is Chinese on a Chinese Mac and English otherwise. In a 1.4.3 build, Brazilian Portuguese selects the game's official pt-BR text. To give only this game another language, set its preferred language, for example `defaults write org.macnativegames.totk AppleLanguages -array pt-BR` (`defaults delete org.macnativegames.totk AppleLanguages` removes it). To override, launch with `TOTK_LANG` for the game (for example `open --env TOTK_LANG=en-US "Tears of the Kingdom.app"`) or `TOTK_UI_LANG=zh` / `en` for the launcher text.

## Where things are

- Saves: `~/Library/Application Support/MacNativeGames/TOTK/profile`
- Shader cache: `~/Library/Application Support/MacNativeGames/TOTK/shader-cache` (delete it to translate everything again)
- Shaders the shared list does not have yet: `~/Library/Application Support/MacNativeGames/TOTK/shader-list-contribution.txt`
- Log: `~/Library/Logs/MacNativeGames/totk.log` (the run before: `totk.previous.log`)
- Mods: `~/Library/Application Support/MacNativeGames/TOTK/mods/<v0|v112|v121|v143>`. Its `manifest.tsv` lists each RomFS file the mod replaces or adds as tab-separated path, size, SHA-256 and the original's SHA-256 (`-` for a file the game does not have); the files sit under the same paths. `python3 games/totk/scripts/make_mod_manifest.py <mods folder> --app <Tears of the Kingdom.app>` writes it, adding files the game lacks; a path that differs from the game's only in upper and lower case stops it (paths are case-sensitive). Only the RomFS (data) side of a mod is loaded: ExeFS parts (extra code modules, IPS patches) are not supported. The game checks every listed file at start and stops on a mismatch, or when a mod file changes while it runs. Delete the folder to play without mods.

## Known issues

- Supports base 1.0.0, or base plus the separate 1.1.2, 1.2.1 or 1.4.3 update NSP/NSZ. Other versions, DLC, combined packages, compressed base games (NSZ/XCZ) and personalized tickets remain unsupported. On iPhone and iPad only 1.4.3 has been tested; places no player has reported can show missing objects, and on an iPhone 14 iOS can close the game when memory runs out (see [iPhone and iPad](#iphone-and-ipad)).
- No online features, no amiibo.
- New shaders can cause compilation stutters. Cache reuse reduces these, but does not guarantee stutter-free gameplay.
- The 79 automated tests cover generated container/update fixtures, relocation formats, work-folder isolation, packaging, desktop migration, shader extraction (BNSH, agl `.sharcb` and game-module shaders), the shared shader list and the players' contribution file, first-import cache preservation, the Metal toolchain lookup and 27 native RomFS path cases. GitHub Actions is configured to run the source tests and the native path parser under the undefined-behavior sanitizer, without game data or keys. A complete Mac build also passed with a local XCI-derived NSP fixture and generated common ticket. An independent retail base NSP and gameplay from that input have not yet been tested.

## 本机测试

已在 **MacBook Air M4 和 Mac mini M4** 上测试。本机测试已收集 **8,582 个着色器**，着色器预热后约 **90 帧/秒，菜单中可达 120 帧/秒**。

以上是此前本机观察，不代表所有版本和场景都能稳定达到该帧率。1.4.3 的场景测量及首次编译卡顿另见[测试记录](docs/v1.4.3-port.md)。

着色器会在游玩过程中自动收集、编译并缓存。再次进入已经去过的场景时，可以复用已有缓存，帧数和流畅度通常会明显改善。**8,582 只是本机测试目前收集到的数量，不是游戏的着色器总数，也不是收集上限**；随着探索更多场景，缓存还会继续增加。

**首次启动的着色器预热：** 构建时从你提供的所选版本游戏数据准备着色器并装进 App：游戏数据里的每个着色器按默认绑定状态各准备一个，再加上[公共着色器清单](docs/shader-list.md)里列出的全部变体。即使用户缓存为空，第一次打开也会导入这批着色器。第一帧前只预热标题画面自己用到的那部分（macOS 编过之后约 2 秒）；其余连同兼容的管线清单，在标题画面后面继续预热，第一次进入世界时最多再等 15 秒。不需要先玩一遍或手动复制缓存。当前 1.4.3 准备 15,266 个。打包时还会把它们为本机的 GPU 编一遍。装有 Xcode 的 Metal 工具链时直接编进 App（1.4.3 在 M4 上约 6 分钟），App 挪到哪里都能用；没有工具链时编进 macOS 的 Metal 缓存（几分钟），这时游戏要从打包时的位置运行，Metal 才找得到它们：之后挪动 App（比如挪进 /Applications）、macOS 清掉了缓存（系统盘写满时会清）、或打包时有别的程序正在用 Metal 的缓存（比如开着游戏，打包时会提示），后台预热都要重新编，需要几分钟，做完之前进入新场景可能卡顿。想放在别处，就用 `-o` 直接打包到那里，详见[准备过程与实测记录](docs/first-launch-shaders.md)。还没有玩家报告过的地方仍可能需要新的变体，Mac 会在游玩时现编（第一次会短暂卡顿），并存进本机缓存，以后启动时复用。游戏还会把公共清单里还没有的变体记进 `shader-list-contribution.txt`，每攒够 500 个问一次要不要用 [GitHub Issue](https://github.com/ly05010419/MacNativeGames/issues/new?template=shader-list.yml) 发送这个文件（点“发送”会打开提交页面并显示文件，拖进去即可）。游戏不会自己上传任何东西。会用 git 的话，也可以把本机缓存并入清单再提 pull request，做法见[清单说明](docs/shader-list.md)。清单只有着色器和管线的标识，不含游戏数据、存档或编译后的着色器；每次打包都用玩家自己的游戏文件生成着色器。


## 需要准备

- Apple 芯片的 Mac，**macOS 26** 或更高（图形用 Metal 4），支持 macOS 27。建议使用 16 GB 或更多内存。
- 除游戏文件外，为工作目录预留约 **25 GB** 空闲空间。成品 App 与工作目录放在**同一个 APFS 卷**上时，大型数据文件可通过克隆共享磁盘空间；无法克隆或输出到其他卷时，还需为 App 副本另留约 **17 GB**。
- 你的《王国之泪》**本体 1.0.0**（`0100F2C0115B6000`），格式为 **XCI 或 NSP**，以及你的 `prod.keys`。构建 **1.1.2、1.2.1 或 1.4.3** 时，通过 `--update` 提供单独的累计更新 NSP 或 NSZ；无需先安装中间版本。NSZ 会先解压并校验其中的 NCA 哈希。DLC 和合并包不支持。
- 使用 NSP 时：除不依赖票据的 NCA 外，包内必须包含通用票据。NSP 不含系统共享字体，需要通过 `--firmware` 指定已解包的固件 NCA 目录，或通过 `--shared-fonts` 提供以前提取的字体。六个字体会与本项目的参考转储核对；来自其他固件版本的有效 BFTTF 字体会按它自身的字节接受并绑定。工作目录中已有且校验通过的字体会自动复用。

## 打包 App

**1. 工具**（只需一次）：Xcode 命令行工具和 [Homebrew](https://brew.sh)。安装构建依赖和获取固定版本源码需要联网：

```sh
xcode-select --install
brew install opus libvpx python@3.14
```

构建 iPhone / iPad App 还需要完整的 **Xcode 26 或更高版本**（包含 iOS 和 Metal 工具链），并安装以下工具：

```sh
brew install xcodegen cmake ninja
```

可选：装有 Xcode 的 Metal 工具链（`xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain`）时，构建会把启动着色器预先编译进 App。Xcode 不在 `/Applications` 也能找到（放在其他卷上，或设置 `DEVELOPER_DIR`）。没有它时，构建会改为把它们编进本机 Metal 缓存里属于 App 所在位置的那一份，这份缓存不跟着 App 走：挪动 App 之后，第一次启动会重新编译。

**2. 下载或克隆本仓库**，在终端中进入 `MacNativeGames` 目录，再运行脚本，给出游戏文件和密钥：

```sh
python3.14 build_app.py ~/Games/totk.xci -k ~/keys/prod.keys
```

使用 NSP 时，还要提供共享字体：

```sh
python3.14 build_app.py ~/Games/totk.nsp -k ~/keys/prod.keys --firmware ~/Games/firmware
# 或复用以前构建时提取的六个 .bfttf 文件：
python3.14 build_app.py ~/Games/totk.nsp -k ~/keys/prod.keys --shared-fonts /path/to/TOTK_build/totk/extracted/firmware/shared-fonts
```

`--firmware` 接受包含 `.nca` 文件的目录（固件压缩包需先解压），也接受已安装固件的 `registered` 目录。`--shared-fonts` 接受包含 `0-standard.bfttf` 至 `5-nintendo-extension.bfttf` 的提取目录。工具不会下载字体或密钥。XCI 默认从其系统更新分区提取字体；如果该分区缺失，也可以使用上述字体选项。默认情况下，两种输入格式最终都生成 macOS `.app`。

要构建 iPhone / iPad IPA，请添加 `--platform ios`，并使用 `.ipa` 输出路径：

```sh
python3.14 build_app.py ~/Games/totk.xci -k ~/keys/prod.keys --platform ios -o ~/Games/TOTK.ipa
```

构建更新版时添加 `--update ~/Games/1.4.3.nsp`；本体为 NSP 时也要继续提供 `--firmware` 或 `--shared-fonts`。首次 iOS 构建会下载并编译适用于设备的 Opus 和 libvpx，并为 iOS 编译着色器种子，因此需要联网和较多临时磁盘空间（全新本体构建建议至少预留 **45 GB**，全新本体加更新包建议预留 **60 GB**）。生成的 IPA 未签名，需使用侧载工具签名和安装，签名时要保留它的权限（它用到提高内存上限）。需要 iOS / iPadOS 26，最低支持 iPhone 14。实测情况见 [iPhone 和 iPad](#iphone-和-ipad)。

不使用 `-o` 时，选定的平台成品会放在游戏文件旁边（Mac 为 `Tears of the Kingdom.app`，iOS 为 `Tears of the Kingdom.ipa`）。加入完整着色器准备前，本地一次本体 1.0.0 Mac 全新构建在 M4 Mac mini 上约 6 分钟（这不是当前构建的耗时预估；耗时受硬件、磁盘和网络影响）：改写主代码模块、解密 17 GB 的游戏数据各约 1 分钟，macOS 把做好的 App 检查一遍要 2–3 分钟。现在的打包还会准备启动着色器（1.4.3 在 M4 上约 3 分钟），再为本机 GPU 编译（再要几分钟；没有 Metal 工具链时，有游戏开着会跳过这一步，并提示）。Mac 打包不需要 .NET 或 CMake，做好的游戏运行时也不需要 Python：着色器翻译器是本仓库自带的原生程序（`games/totk/prebuilt`）。所有中间文件都在游戏文件旁边的工作目录里（`TOTK_build`，或用 `--work` 指定），再运行一次会复用已经做好的部分。

提取的程序模块、改写后的模块、RomFS 和共享字体会与所选版本的 `games/totk/assets/expected-v1.0.0.json`、`expected-v1.1.2.json`、`expected-v1.2.1.json` 或 `expected-v1.4.3.json` 中的哈希核对；预编译着色器翻译器另有 SHA-256 校验。不匹配时停止构建，但有一个例外：同一版本的另一份真实零售转储会被接受——它的 `main.npdm` 改用任天堂的 ACID 签名校验（`npdm_signed()`），而不是固定的哈希；其固件的共享字体则检查是否为有效的 BFTTF 结构，并按实际 SHA-256 绑定。密钥的值不会被打印。

大型更新版 App 的完整签名和校验还可能多用几分钟；日志持续报告进度时，请等待构建完成。

**3. 游玩：** 在访达里打开 App。构建结束时会以 `--check` 模式启动启动器，检查游戏可执行文件是否存在，并让 macOS 执行首次启动检查；这一步不进行游戏游玩测试。App 可以留在原位置，也可以移到 `/Applications`；挪动之后的第一次启动要在后台重新编着色器（Metal 的缓存不跟着 App 走），想放在 `/Applications` 就用 `-o` 直接打包到那里。拷贝到另一个卷可能额外占用磁盘空间，并触发 macOS 再次检查，期间可能没有窗口。第一次进入游戏会校验游戏数据（本地测试约 20 秒）。首次遇到的着色器可能造成编译卡顿，缓存可减少后续访问时的重复工作。


### 构建 1.1.2、1.2.1 或 1.4.3

```sh
python3.14 build_app.py ~/Games/totk.xci -k ~/keys/prod.keys --update ~/Games/1.1.2.nsp
# 也可以使用 NSZ 更新包：
python3.14 build_app.py ~/Games/totk.xci -k ~/keys/prod.keys --update ~/Games/1.1.2.nsz
# 也可从同一本体直接构建 1.2.1 或 1.4.3：
python3.14 build_app.py ~/Games/totk.xci -k ~/keys/prod.keys --update ~/Games/1.2.1.nsp
python3.14 build_app.py ~/Games/totk.xci -k ~/keys/prod.keys --update ~/Games/1.4.3.nsz
# 本体为 NSP 时，继续提供上文的 --firmware 或 --shared-fonts。
```

仍然只生成同一个 **Tears of the Kingdom.app**，包内只含选定版本。先退出正在运行的游戏，再用相同 `-o` 路径重新构建即可替换旧 App，不增加第二个游戏入口或版本选择菜单。窗口标题显示选定版本，例如 **Ver. 1.4.3**。不加 `--update` 时仍构建 1.0.0。

无需另外下载 1.2.1 / 1.4.3 运行时表或着色器缓存。构建流程会根据你提供的游戏数据生成对应版本的运行时表和首启着色器种子，并将种子放进 App。仓库已包含各个支持的更新版的补丁代码和校验哈希；外部只需准备自己的本体、更新包和密钥。

首次完整更新构建建议预留约 **40 GB**，已缓存本体数据时还需约 **19 GB** 空间，App 需放在同一 APFS 卷。合并时通过原始容器的限定区间读取本体 NCA，只临时提取较小的更新 NCA，并校验全部 IVFC 层；工具会获取固定提交的 [hactool](https://github.com/SciresM/hactool)，用 clang / make 编译。临时票据文件仅当前用户可读，合并结束即清理；密钥值不进入命令行或日志。

存档继续保存在原 profile 目录。首次启动更新版前，App 会在旁边完整备份为 `profile-before-1.1.2`、`profile-before-1.2.1` 或 `profile-before-1.4.3`；备份失败就不启动。需要回退旧版本时保留并使用这份备份，不能假定新版存档向下兼容。

如需保留唯一桌面入口，可用附带的安装脚本建立 App 链接：

```sh
python3.14 games/totk/tools/install_desktop_entry.py --app "/路径/Tears of the Kingdom.app"
```

替换旧开发启动器时，脚本会将旧存档完整复制并校验到下列标准用户目录，同时建立升级备份；原存档保留，旧启动器归档后不再作为第二个 App 入口。已有且内容不同的标准存档不会被覆盖。

来源运行时已通过 Mac 基础检查：读档、移动 / 跳跃、菜单 / 地图、2K、保存重读及死亡重试。全地图、长局与 1.0 / 1.1.2 公平性能对比仍待测试；前面的帧率观察不是对 1.1.2 的性能承诺。打包验证范围见[构建记录](docs/how-it-works.md#112-validation)。

### iPhone 和 iPad

1.4.3 已在 **iPhone 14（iOS 26.6.1）** 和 **A16 芯片的 iPad（iPadOS 26.7.1）** 上实际游玩，两台都是在 Xcode 里用个人开发团队签名安装的。1.0.0、1.1.2 和 1.2.1 没有在 iOS 上测过。

- **第一次启动：** App 先校验游戏数据（约 15 秒），再导入随 App 准备的着色器，有进度条。iPhone 14 上约 3 分钟后出现标题画面；之后的启动约 8 秒出标题。
- **画面：** 游戏以掌机模式运行，和 Switch 不接底座时一样：1280×720。
- **着色器：** iPhone 和 iPad 不能在游玩时翻译着色器。App 里没有的着色器变体，对应的绘制会被跳过，所以还没有玩家报告过的地方可能缺少物体。设备会把缺的记进 `shader-list-contribution.txt`（“文件”App › 我的 iPhone › Tears of the Kingdom），玩的时候游戏从不因此打扰你。设备连着打包它的那台 Mac（线连或同一 Wi‑Fi）时，Mac 每 10 分钟检查一次，每多 500 个问一次要不要用 [GitHub Issue](https://github.com/ly05010419/MacNativeGames/issues/new?template=shader-list.yml) 发送（`games/totk/ios/tools/shader_contrib_watch.py`，打包 iOS 版时自动安装；`--no-shader-reminder` 不装，`shader_contrib_watch.py uninstall` 卸掉）；并入[公共着色器清单](docs/shader-list.md)后，下一次打包时所有人就都有了。有 Mac 的话，也可以用 `games/totk/ios/tools/fill_shaders.py` 马上翻译这些变体并推回设备。
- **内存：** 在 iPhone 14 上游戏占用接近 4 GB，接近手机能给它的上限。在复杂的区域玩几分钟后，手机内存耗尽时 iOS 可能会关掉游戏（iPhone 14 上出现过两次，都在约 8 分钟时）。降低 iOS 上的内存占用是下一步要做的事。

## 操作

在 Mac 上，macOS 能识别的手柄（如 DualSense、Xbox 手柄）会映射为 Switch Pro 手柄。PlayStation 和 Xbox 手柄的四个面键按位置映射，和游戏里的按键提示位置一致：右边是 A、下边是 B、上边是 X、左边是 Y（圆圈 / 叉 / 三角 / 方块；Xbox 的 B / A / Y / X）。任天堂手柄按标签映射。设置 `TOTK_FACE_BUTTONS=label` 可以让所有手柄都按标签映射。震动和体感需要手柄及 macOS 提供对应能力，并非所有手柄都有陀螺仪。Mac 键盘映射按美式布局对应的物理键位：

| 按键 | Switch | | 按键 | Switch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W A S D | 左摇杆 | | 方向键 | 右摇杆 |
| J | A | | K、空格 | B |
| I | X（跳） | | U | Y（攻击） |
| Q / E | L / R | | Option / Shift | ZL / ZR |
| F T H G | 十字键 左 / 上 / 右 / 下 | | Z / C | 左 / 右摇杆按下 |
| Return | +（菜单） | | Tab、Esc | −（地图） |

手柄布局（Mac）：默认按位置对应 Switch 的布局，每种手柄都是右边的面键为 A、下边为 B、上边为 X、左边为 Y（任天堂手柄按标签，结果相同；`TOTK_FACE_BUTTONS=label` 让 PlayStation、Xbox 手柄改为按标签）。要改任何按钮，在 `~/Library/Application Support/MacNativeGames/TOTK/controls.txt` 写 `实体按钮 = Switch 按钮` 的行；没写的按钮保持默认，`#` 开始注释，`none` 表示不用这个按钮。实体按钮按位置命名：`south` `east` `west` `north`（面键），`l1` `r1` `l2` `r2` `l3` `r3`，`menu`（Options / Menu），`view`（Create / View），`up` `down` `left` `right`（十字键），`touchpad`（DualSense / DualShock 4 的触控板按下，默认不用；`touchpad = minus` 打开普尔亚平板）。Switch 按钮：`a` `b` `x` `y` `l` `r` `zl` `zr` `plus` `minus` `lstick` `rstick` `up` `down` `left` `right`。默认布局和下面这个文件相同（按位置）：

```
east = a
south = b
north = x
west = y
```

要不按住就跑，可以让两行驱动奔跑键：`south = b tap`（像 GTA 一样连续点按下方面键，每次按下保持 400 毫秒）或 `l3 = b toggle`（按一下左摇杆再移动；摇杆回到中间时停止）。可选的模式写在 Switch 按钮后面：`hold`（默认，按住时保持）、`tap`、`toggle`，以及 `aim <开火键>`：按住时保持，但开火键也按下时松开。`l2 = zr aim r2` 用 L2 拉弓、R2 射出，L2 松开时 R2 才按自己那一行生效。Switch 的 B 键随情境变化：攀爬时按住 B 会松手，所以攀爬时如果 toggle 还开着，角色会掉下来。攀爬前先松开摇杆，或改用 `tap`。

启动器每次启动都会检查这个文件，有错时弹窗指出第一行错误。删除文件即恢复默认布局。

仅限 Mac 的额外按键：**1** 同时隐藏或重新显示所有屏幕提示（FPS、着色器计数、系统负载和快捷键说明，集中在窗口右上角的一个小框里；`TOTK_HUD=corners` 恢复为画面四角显示）；**2** 补帧（关 → 30+30 → 刷新率一半 → 不限帧），**3** 循环切换画质（MetalFX 2K → 原生 2K → 关闭），**4** 21:9 超宽屏开 / 关（1.2.1 和 1.4.3：镜头两侧看到更多，画面铺满更宽的窗口；`TOTK_ASPECT=32:9` 或 `3440x1440` 换成别的比例并以宽屏启动；HUD、菜单和地图保持原比例，放在窗口中间的 16:9 区域，地图两侧是黑边；跟着世界物体走的标记还没往两侧挪）。快捷键说明会显示当前补帧和画质档位，两种提示布局都每半秒刷新一次。MetalFX 默认关闭，只有按 **3** 手动切换到该模式才会启用；放大窗口不会自动开启。文字输入（给马取名）直接用 Mac 键盘。iPhone / iPad 使用触屏控件或兼容手柄，不会显示 Mac 的 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 快捷键提示。触屏按 Switch 手柄排布：左上 L、ZL，右上 R、ZR，中间 − 和 +，左边十字键，右边 A、B、X、Y。十字键在左摇杆上方，A、B、X、Y 在右摇杆上方，L3、R3（按下摇杆）在左下角和右下角。在左半屏避开按钮的地方按住拖动是左摇杆，在右半屏是转镜头（右摇杆）；摇杆以手指按下的位置为中心。接上手柄时触屏控件自动隐藏：碰一下屏幕就会显示，可以照常使用，手指离开 3 秒后再次隐藏。

原生 2K 将游戏合成画布和 UI 改为 2560×1440，3D 场景仍由游戏独立的渲染比例控制，并非强制所有内部通道以 1440p 渲染。手动 MetalFX 在较小窗口中也可使用，输出放大会跟随实际窗口尺寸，包括 4K。

语言：游戏和启动器自身的文字（启动画面、着色器预热进度、提示叠层、键盘输入提示）跟随 Mac 的系统语言。启动器文字在中文系统上显示中文，其他语言显示英文。1.4.3 版本中，巴西葡萄牙语会选择游戏官方的 pt-BR 文本。只想让本游戏使用另一种语言时，可设置它的首选语言，例如 `defaults write org.macnativegames.totk AppleLanguages -array pt-BR`（`defaults delete org.macnativegames.totk AppleLanguages` 可撤销）。如需指定，可用 `TOTK_LANG` 设置游戏语言（例如 `open --env TOTK_LANG=zh-Hans "Tears of the Kingdom.app"`），用 `TOTK_UI_LANG=zh` / `en` 设置启动器文字。

## 文件位置

- 存档：`~/Library/Application Support/MacNativeGames/TOTK/profile`
- 着色器缓存：`~/Library/Application Support/MacNativeGames/TOTK/shader-cache`（删掉会全部重新翻译）
- 公共清单里还没有的着色器：`~/Library/Application Support/MacNativeGames/TOTK/shader-list-contribution.txt`
- 日志：`~/Library/Logs/MacNativeGames/totk.log`（上一次运行：`totk.previous.log`）
- 模组：`~/Library/Application Support/MacNativeGames/TOTK/mods/<v0|v112|v121|v143>`。其中的 `manifest.tsv` 以制表符分隔列出模组替换或新增的每个 RomFS 文件：路径、大小、SHA-256 和原文件的 SHA-256（游戏里没有的新文件写 `-`）；文件按相同路径存放。可用 `python3 games/totk/scripts/make_mod_manifest.py <模组文件夹> --app <Tears of the Kingdom.app>` 生成，游戏里没有的文件会作为新增文件写入；只是大小写和游戏里的路径不同的会报错（路径区分大小写）。只加载模组的 RomFS（数据）部分，ExeFS 部分（额外的代码模块、IPS 补丁）不支持。游戏启动时校验所有列出的文件，不一致即停止；游戏运行中模组文件被改动也会停止。删除该文件夹即可不带模组运行。

## 已知问题

- 支持本体 1.0.0，或本体加单独的 1.1.2 / 1.2.1 / 1.4.3 更新（NSP/NSZ）。其他版本、DLC、合并包、压缩本体（NSZ/XCZ）和个性化票据仍不支持。iPhone 和 iPad 上只测过 1.4.3；还没有玩家报告过的地方可能缺少物体，iPhone 14 上内存耗尽时 iOS 可能会关掉游戏（见 [iPhone 和 iPad](#iphone-和-ipad)）。
- 没有联网功能，没有 amiibo。
- 首次遇到新着色器可能出现编译卡顿，缓存能减少重复编译，但不保证完全没有卡顿。
- 79 项自动测试覆盖生成的容器 / 更新样本、重定位格式、工作目录隔离、打包、桌面入口迁移、着色器提取（BNSH、agl 的 `.sharcb` 和游戏程序里的着色器）、公共着色器清单和玩家的贡献文件、首次导入的缓存保留、Metal 工具链查找及 27 个原生 RomFS 路径用例。GitHub Actions 已配置为运行源码测试，并在未定义行为检查（UBSan）下运行原生路径解析器，不需要游戏数据或密钥；另使用本地 XCI 构造、附带生成通用票据的 NSP 测试副本完成完整 Mac 打包。尚未验证独立的零售本体 NSP，也未测试从该类输入构建后的实际游玩。

## 工作原理

见 [docs/how-it-works.md](docs/how-it-works.md)。

已做的性能实验、待办与对比方法见 [Mac 性能待做](docs/performance-followups.md)。

## 致谢

- **[d2r-mobile](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile)**（MIT）为《暗黑破坏神 II：狱火重生》开发了这套原生运行 Switch 游戏的方法：这里的 NSO 改写器、Horizon 宿主和 Metal 上的 NVN 层都从它的通用部分起步。
- **[nxnative](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative)**：“用户自己的游戏文件 + 一个脚本出包”和 NSP 通用票据读取的做法借鉴自它；本项目只构建 Mac App。
- **Ryujinx**（MIT）：它的着色器翻译器（`vendor/ryujinx`）把游戏的 Maxwell 着色器转成 SPIR-V，它的系统服务代码也是参考。加上本项目的补丁和着色器服务，用 .NET NativeAOT 预先编成原生程序 `games/totk/prebuilt/macos-arm64/totk_xlate`；改了翻译器用 `games/totk/tools/totk_xlate/publish_native.sh` 重编（要 .NET 10 SDK，只有开发者需要）。
- **[SPIRV-Cross](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Cross)**（Apache-2.0）把 SPIR-V 转成 Metal 着色语言；打包时按固定提交取得，用 clang 编。
- **deko3d**（zlib）：贴图布局尺寸。**bcdec**：BC 贴图解码。**libopus**、**libvpx**（BSD，来自 Homebrew）：音频和预渲染影片。

## 许可证

MIT（见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)）。第三方代码保留各自的许可证：[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)。

# Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection for Windows

**Uncharted 1, 2 and 3 from the PS4 collection running natively on Windows 10 and 11, by [SuperMedo](https://github.com/Supermedo).** Mohammed Albarghouthi

Same idea as my [Bloodborne port](https://github.com/Supermedo/bloodborne_pc): the original PS4 game
code runs directly on your PC and the graphics are translated to Vulkan. Unpack the zip, start
`Uncharted.exe`, pick your game folder, choose a game and press **PLAY**.

**[Download the latest version](https://github.com/Supermedo/uncharted_pc/releases/latest)** · **[Join the Discord]([https://discord.gg/yTMG8c4Bqm](https://discord.gg/s3RgH6cRfJ))**

> **No game files are included.** You need your own decrypted dump of the collection
> (CUSA02343, CUSA02320, ...: the folder with eboot.bin, big2-ps4_Shipping.elf,
> big3-ps4_Shipping.elf, sce_sys, u1data, u2data and u3data).
> This project is not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment or Naughty Dog.

## Features

- All three games from one launcher: Drake's Fortune, Among Thieves and Drake's Deception.
- 60 FPS like on PS4, or 120 FPS (higher rates are experimental).
- Anti-aliasing with TAA, AMD FSR 3.1, AMD FSR 4 or NVIDIA DLSS (DLAA).
- Frame generation: AMD FSR 3 (any GPU) or NVIDIA DLSS (RTX 40 2x, RTX 50 up to 4x).
- Keyboard, mouse and controller together, all remappable. Mouse look in U3.
- Add to Steam and desktop shortcuts from the launcher, automatic updates.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 (1903 or later) or Windows 11, 64-bit.
- A graphics card with Vulkan 1.3 and a current driver.
- About 8 GB of free memory (RAM + page file).

## Known problems

- **Uncharted 3, Cartagena square (chapter 2):** at high frame rates (240 Hz setting, ~80 FPS)
  the game could freeze and close with "GPU crash: the graphics device was lost". It came from
  the speed fix for that area and is fixed in 0.3. If it still happens to you, set Frame rate to
  60 on the Display page and open an issue with your `user\last_run.log`.
- **Uncharted 3:** green or black shapes flash for a single frame on some characters (Sully's
  shirt in Cartagena). It happens in shadPS4 too, so it's a shader translation problem. Not fixed yet.
- **Crash with "ASSERTION: GetRenderFrameParams(frameToFreeInstancesFor)->m_gfxEopTick":** the
  game got too many frames ahead of the GPU side while it was busy (building shaders on a first
  run). 0.3.1 holds the game at most one frame ahead, like on PS4. If you still see it, open an
  issue with your log.
- Frame rates above 120 are experimental.

## Building

MSYS2 CLANG64 on Windows: `bash build.sh` builds `out\bb-probe.exe`, and
`bash packaging/windows/package.sh` makes `dist\uncharted-windows` and the zip.

## Credits

Built on [bbport](https://github.com/deadinside28/bloodborne_pc), the native Linux port of
Bloodborne by deadinside28, and on the [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4)
renderer. Video decoding (Videodec2) and the DLSS bridge come from
[IFreemz/shadPS4-Bloodborne-DLSS-FSR](https://github.com/IFreemz/shadPS4-Bloodborne-DLSS-FSR).
Thanks to Mindro for the shadPS4 Uncharted build that showed which problems to look for.

Also used: [FSR-Vulkan](https://github.com/FireBurn/FSR-Vulkan) and the AMD FidelityFX SDK (FSR),
FSR 4 assets from [FireBurn/Q2RTX](https://github.com/FireBurn/Q2RTX), the
[NVIDIA DLSS SDK](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS) (`nvngx_dlss.dll` under NVIDIA's license),
[LibAtrac9](https://github.com/Thealexbarney/LibAtrac9), [SDL3](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL),
[FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org), [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui),
[sirit](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/sirit), [magic_enum](https://github.com/Neargye/magic_enum),
[xbyak](https://github.com/herumi/xbyak),
[Vulkan Memory Allocator](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator),
[MSYS2](https://www.msys2.org) / [LLVM](https://llvm.org), [PyInstaller](https://pyinstaller.org),
[Pillow](https://python-pillow.org) and the Cinzel font (SIL Open Font License).

NVIDIA, GeForce RTX and DLSS are trademarks of NVIDIA Corporation. The default covers and the
icon are original artwork; no official art is included.

## License

GNU GPL v2 or later ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). Third-party components keep their own licenses
(see `licenses\` in the download).
